sections.title: Latest arXiv biology batch: five notable papers on RNA design, spatial cell states, molecular interactions, and medical-image explanations
sections.abstract: The 26 November 2026 Quantitative Biology listing has five relevant papers selected here by scope and reported evidence, not measured popularity; arXiv has no official trending chart and its biomedical coverage is incomplete.
sections.claimed_contribution: The report summarizes recent methods spanning molecular design and modeling, spatial omics, and medical-image classification.
sections.unique_caveat: The supplied signal collector returned no candidates, and its stated interval does not match the papers shown in the official listing.

sections.title: KnitNet: Learning to Search at Inference Time for Exact RNA Inverse Design
sections.abstract: KnitNet uses verifier feedback to iteratively repair candidate RNA sequences; the authors report higher exact-fold solve rates on five secondary-structure benchmarks and improved 3D self-consistency in computational tests.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report an average 21-percentage-point increase in exact solves versus continued sampling with 70% less time-to-solve across five secondary-structure benchmarks, plus improved 3D structural self-consistency and faster inference than per-target RL.
sections.unique_caveat: Computational benchmark results only; the abstract reports no biochemical folding or functional validation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: No candidate-level score or attention counts were present; selected for direct RNA-design relevance, not popularity.

sections.title: Resolving cell states in spatial transcriptomics with SCATTER
sections.abstract: SCATTER jointly estimates cell-type proportions and within-cell-type expression from spatial transcriptomic spots, using spatial context and single-cell reference profiles.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report higher measured-expression correlations than three comparators for 82.8–99.8% of evaluated gene–cell-type pairs across five pseudo-spot benchmarks, plus analyses of breast cancer, multiple-sclerosis, and colorectal-cancer tissue data.
sections.unique_caveat: Much of the quantitative comparison uses pseudo-spots; tissue applications are computational analyses, not independent biological validation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: No candidate-level score or attention counts were present; selected for spatial-omics relevance and reported benchmark/tissue analyses.

sections.title: Exclusion and internal structure in the association/dissociation kinetics of DNA-binding proteins in the fast diffusion limit
sections.abstract: The paper develops a coarse-grained stochastic model for DNA-binding proteins that combines footprint exclusion, diffusion, and conformational switching, and fits it to previously measured RPA–ssDNA dynamics.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors derive an effective Markov model and mean-field approximation, then use multisegment binding states to model facilitated exchange and the trade-off between affinity and remodeling.
sections.unique_caveat: Theoretical/coarse-grained model fitted to previously measured RPA dynamics, not a new binding experiment; generalization to other proteins remains to be tested.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: No candidate-level score or attention counts were present; selected for molecular-biophysics relevance and its stated fit to experimental RPA data.

sections.title: From the Deterministic Hook Effect to Stochastic Reliability in Ternary Complex Formation
sections.abstract: Deterministic equations and stochastic simulations show how mediator dose, compartment size, and copy-number thresholds can alter ternary-complex reliability in a minimal binding model.
sections.claimed_contribution: The author reports that small simulated volumes can fail to form sufficient complexes despite favorable deterministic dose-response, and that volume, thresholds, completion rates, and breakup rates alter the reliable dose range.
sections.unique_caveat: Minimal deterministic/stochastic models and a catalytic extension; no experimental system or clinical outcomes are reported in the abstract.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: No candidate-level score or attention counts were present; selected for direct molecular-binding relevance.

sections.title: DDxBasis: Explaining Frozen Foundation Encoder-based Medical Classification by Exact Differential Diagnosis
sections.abstract: DDxBasis decomposes frozen-image-encoder classifications into diagnosis contrasts and case findings, with tests across five medical-image datasets.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report exact concept-level decomposition of model decisions and performance competitive with published domain-specific methods across five datasets; they also report recovering label-free structure and exposing shortcuts.
sections.unique_caveat: Retrospective model and dataset results do not establish clinical utility or prospective performance; external-site validation remains necessary.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: No candidate-level score or attention counts were present; included for biomedical-method relevance, not popularity. Original v1 date is 2026-11-24.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.abstract: The selected papers share computational and mathematical approaches to RNA design and molecular interactions; SCATTER and DDxBasis each illustrate a distinct single-paper application rather than a broad field-wide trend.
sections.claimed_contribution: The corpus connects sequence design, mechanistic binding models, cell-resolved spatial expression, and interpretable biomedical prediction.
sections.unique_caveat: The empty attention pool and small, relevance-selected sample cannot establish field-level popularity or a broad shift.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.abstract: Useful follow-ups include experimental RNA structure/function assays, spatial transcriptomic validation with independent cell-type measurements, empirical tests of molecular binding models across reaction conditions, and external-site evaluation of image-classifier explanations.
sections.claimed_contribution: These proposed validation steps are grounded in the evidence boundaries described by KnitNet, SCATTER, the two molecular-interaction models, and DDxBasis.
sections.unique_caveat: These are research proposals derived from preprints, not clinical guidance or claims that a direction is novel or tractable.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.abstract: The selected batch is strongest in computational and mathematical methods for RNA design, molecular binding, and cell-resolved expression, with one interpretable medical-imaging method.
sections.claimed_contribution: Treat this as a relevance-ranked snapshot of a small arXiv listing, not as a measured popularity ranking.
sections.unique_caveat: The signal collector returned no candidate-level attention data, and its reported date window conflicts with the current official listing.
